Red flags: 2023 dispute with Italy over the Discobolus Lancellotti and its base
- Stéphane Verger, director of the Museo Nazionale Romano, wrote to the head of the Glyptothek asking for the return of the statue's 18th-century marble base; the Discobolus was bought by Germany in 1938 on orders from Mussolini and Bottai, held in Munich and returned to Italy on 16 November 1948 (Open, 2 December 2023).
- Open published the Munich reply: "Non sono nella condizioni di abbandonare la nostra rivendicazione legale di una restituzione del Discoboo al nostro museo" ("I am not in a position to abandon our legal claim to a return of the Discobolus to our museum", translated), and "Il rimpatrio in Italia ha violato la legge, secondo l'opinione legale dello stato bavarese e del nostro museo" ("The repatriation to Italy broke the law, in the legal opinion of the Bavarian state and of our museum", translated) (Open, 2 December 2023).
- Italy's culture minister Gennaro Sangiuliano said "devono passare sul mio cadavere" ("they will have to pass over my dead body", translated) and asked for the base as well (Open, 2 December 2023).
- On 5 December 2023 the Ministry of Culture said the Discobolus is "patrimonio della Nazione e proprietà dello Stato italiano" ("heritage of the Nation and property of the Italian State", translated) and will stay in the Museo Nazionale Romano; after meeting the German ambassador Hans-Dieter Lucas, Sangiuliano said the Berlin government was not seeking the statue, called the Munich director's letter unacceptable and said the director owed an apology (Italian Ministry of Culture, 5 December 2023) (state outlet).
- Florian Knauss, director of the Glyptothek, told Finestre sull'Arte that "the Glyptothek has not requested the return of the Lancellotti Disk sculpture and does not intend to do so" (Finestre sull'Arte, 5 December 2023).
- On 11 December 2023 the Uffizi director Eike Schmidt said Germany must return the base to Rome as soon as possible; the Glyptothek said talks on the base were going on and its future was open (Abendzeitung, 11 December 2023). Knauss said he and Verger wanted to talk soon and that he was "fermamente convinto che raggiungeremo un accordo amichevole" ("firmly convinced that we will reach an amicable agreement", translated) (Libero, 12 December 2023).

SOURCES
- https://www.open.online/2023/12/02/discobolo-germania-italia-sangiuliano/
- https://cultura.gov.it/comunicato/25618 (state outlet)
- https://www.finestresullarte.info/en/news/lancellotti-discobolo-case-no-request-for-return-from-germany
- https://www.abendzeitung-muenchen.de/muenchen/uffizien-chef-muenchen-soll-sockel-von-diskobolos-statue-zurueckgeben-art-946237
- https://www.liberoquotidiano.it/news/italia/37817547/discobolo-lancelotti-italia-germania-basamento/

Red flags: 2023 plan to replace the museum, dropped in 2024
- In December 2023 the Culture, Sports and Tourism Bureau proposed moving the Science Museum into the Heritage Museum's Sha Tin building, freeing the Science Museum's Tsim Sha Tsui site for a new museum of national achievements and development (The Standard, 7 March 2024).
- Lawmaker Edward Leung Hei said the government plan was for the Heritage Museum to be demolished and rebuilt as the new Science Museum, due for completion in 2031; he said he was concerned whether the government could find another location for the Heritage Museum, and that officials had promised a separate new museum focused on pop culture (The Standard, 8 December 2023).
- A change.org petition started on 9 December 2023 by the artist Loretta Lau condemned the decision to abandon the museum, said it "is bound to result in the loss of a substantial amount of crucial archives and artworks" and asked for an alternative site; it had 800 supporters when it closed (change.org) (advocacy source).
- On 7 March 2024 the Leisure and Cultural Services Department said the Science Museum would stay in Tsim Sha Tsui and the government was looking for a separate site for the new museum; The Standard reported that the Heritage Museum "will not be axed" (The Standard, 7 March 2024).

SOURCES
- https://www.thestandard.com.hk/news/article/211217/Seamless-transition-in-Science-Museum-relocation-plan-says-lawmaker
- https://www.thestandard.com.hk/news/article/214140/Science-Museum-to-stay-in-TST
- https://www.change.org/p/strongly-condemn-the-hksar-gov-s-unjust-decision-to-abandon-the-hong-kong-heritage-museum (advocacy source)

WIDER CONTEXT
- In November 2019 about 50 actors employed under a collective agreement were not paid their October wages; after an emergency meeting the actors announced they would strike within 14 days if not paid, and the theatre owed actors about 2 million shekels (Maariv, Yuval Bagno, 17 November 2019).
- The actors' union SHaM filed an urgent motion at the Tel Aviv Regional Labour Court against the theatre, its CEO Odelia Friedman and its CFO Benny Tzarfati over union dues deducted from actors' pay and not passed on; the theatre's management said the Finance Ministry had not transferred the funding allocated to it by law (Maariv, 17 November 2019).
- In September 2019 the company Power Dialing applied to have the theatre liquidated (Maariv, 17 November 2019).
